samples: This program reads a list of user records from the file data/users.json, keeps only those who are active and at least 18 years old, and prints their e-mail addresses one per line, ordered by user name, followed by a count of how many were found. It only needs permission to read files and write to the console, and it fails with an error if the file can't be read or isn't valid JSON for the expected user format (including an invalid e-mail address or a negative age). The input path is hard-coded in the main entry point, so you would need to edit it, or reuse the filtering function directly, to point it at a different file.

This program reads a list of users from the file "data/users.json" and checks that each user has a plausible e-mail address and a non-negative age. It then prints the e-mail addresses of active users aged 18 or over, one per line and ordered by user name, followed by a count of how many there are. It only needs permission to read files and write to the console, and it fails with a file or JSON error if the file is missing or malformed.

This program reads a list of user accounts from the file `data/users.json`, keeps only those who are active and at least 18 years old, and prints their e-mail addresses one per line, ordered by user name. It finishes by printing a count of how many active adults were found. It only reads from the filesystem and writes to the console, and it fails with a file or JSON error if the file is missing or malformed. Each user's e-mail must look like a plausible address and each age must be non-negative.

This program reads a list of user accounts from the file "data/users.json" and checks that each one has a valid e-mail format and a non-negative age. It then prints the e-mail addresses of active users aged 18 or over, ordered by user name, one per line, followed by a count of how many were found. It only reads from the filesystem and writes to the console, and it stops with an error if the file is missing or its contents are not valid user data.

This program reads a list of user accounts from the file `data/users.json`, keeps only those who are active and at least 18 years old, and prints their e-mail addresses one per line, ordered by user name. It ends with a count of how many such adults were found. It only reads from the filesystem and writes to the console, and it stops with an error if the file can't be read or isn't valid user JSON, including when an age is negative or an e-mail address doesn't look plausible.
